claims.text: A hierarchical microstructure combining coarse and fine grains can simultaneously increase the strength and ductility of eutectic high-entropy alloys.
Introducing a hierarchical coarse/fine-grained microstructure changes the grain-size distribution and grain-boundary interactions.
Fine-grained regions enhance strength through the Hall–Petch effect.
Coarse-grained regions improve ductility by permitting more extensive plastic deformation.
The hierarchical alloy will have greater strength than an otherwise comparable eutectic high-entropy alloy with a conventional non-hierarchical microstructure.
The hierarchical alloy will have greater ductility than an otherwise comparable eutectic high-entropy alloy with a conventional non-hierarchical microstructure.
The magnitude of the strength and ductility improvements depends on the grain-size distribution and alloy composition.
The effectiveness of hierarchical microstructure design may be limited by alloy composition, processing conditions, and application-specific requirements.
The optimal combination of coarse and fine grains for maximizing strength and ductility is unknown.
